output.claim: Under the explicit ledger contract below, atomic, durable idempotency prevents more than one committed transfer for the same scoped key, including concurrent retries, acknowledgment loss, and crash recovery. If every attempt for one intended operation uses that key, this gives at-most-one commitment for that operation—not guaranteed completion, correct authorization, timely settlement, or end-to-end task success. The specification and paired oracle truth table below distinguish those properties. This is an analytical specification, not an executed experiment or measured architectural benefit.
output.method: Specify a small ledger, client retry policy, independent outcome oracle, and deterministic paired fault schedules. Hypothesis for a future experiment: stable-key atomic deduplication reduces duplicate commitments after ambiguous timeouts without unacceptable omission, latency, or cost regressions. The discriminating analytical case is a committed request whose acknowledgment is lost: baseline retries can commit twice, whereas the specified intervention replays one durable receipt. Negative controls include dropped requests, missed receipt deadlines, and unauthorized requests; contract-breaking controls include regenerated keys, early record deletion, and non-atomic effect/record writes. Both arms must use isolated identical snapshots, identical authorization and settlement rules, fixed model/prompt versions and resource ceilings, and the same retry policy; baseline ignores the otherwise identical key field. Safeguard overhead counts against the intervention budget. No runtime is available, so no program or execution is requested. The current action addresses the specification portion of the unresolved ledger/oracle obligation; implementation, audit, inference calibration, and empirical effectiveness remain open.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Scope, economic effect, and authorization
reasoning_steps.argument: One task intends one transfer p*=(run, operation, source, recipient, positive integer amount, currency). Integer minor units avoid rounding ambiguity. A trusted fixture issues a grant g binding the principal, exact p*, and commit-valid interval [0,E]. The expected intent comes from this fixture, not from an agent-supplied label. Authorization is checked at the commitment linearization point, including revocation, account ownership, and sufficient funds. A grant permits repeated matching submissions during its interval; it is deliberately not a one-use token. Otherwise a one-use authorization service would itself supply the duplicate-prevention intervention. The fixture permits no grant renewal. Commitment atomically posts balanced debit/credit entries; settlement subsequently marks that same transaction final and never posts another debit. This is a closed ledger, not an unmodeled external payment rail.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Minimal auditable state
reasoning_steps.argument: The state is (balances, grants/revocations, transaction log L, deduplication map D, request queue, response queue, client journal). Each transaction contains a unique txid, exact payload, grant identity/version, authorization result, commit sequence/time, and status COMMITTED or SETTLED. D maps a scoped key K to the complete payload and durable committed receipt. Requests have distinct attempt IDs but share an operation identity. Their lifecycle is SENT -> DROPPED or QUEUED -> REJECTED, REPLAYED, or COMMITTED. Responses separately become DELIVERED, DELAYED, or LOST. Client journal entries record the intended payload/key before sending, attempt counts, observed receipts, and final output. Authoritative server events record validation, commitment, replay/conflict, recovery, and settlement; transport fault events record drops and delays. Economic events and their deduplication records must survive the same crashes. The oracle reads server state and the fault schedule, not merely the client's journal.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Key scope, binding, and lifetime
reasoning_steps.argument: Define K=(isolated-run epoch, tenant, authenticated principal, transfer-endpoint version, opaque key). One intended operation receives one key, durably journaled before its first send and reused after every timeout or client restart. Distinct operations require distinct keys. D binds K to exact canonical payload equality, including operation ID and all economic fields; equality is not inferred solely from an unchecked hash. Reuse with a different payload returns KEY_CONFLICT and performs no write. Lookup and receipt replay require current read authorization; possession of a key is not authentication. Records survive restart, failover, and snapshot recovery and have no TTL while the namespace exists. Namespace disposal is allowed only with permanent rejection of its old epochs, including restored replicas. A production retention interval would instead need a justified upper bound on every possible replay and restore path; the agent retry deadline alone is insufficient.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Atomic server transition and its baseline
reasoning_steps.argument: For intervention A, Execute(K,p,g) first authenticates access. In one serializable durable transaction: if D[K] exists with p, return its recorded receipt without an economic write; if it exists with a different payload, reject; otherwise recheck current authorization, commit-valid time, and funds, then atomically append one balanced transaction and insert D[K]=(p,receipt). A crash exposes either both writes or neither. Concurrent requests linearize through this transaction; there is no independently durable 'key reserved, effect unfinished' state. Rejected attempts do not reserve keys or cache negative results. A receipt replay may occur after grant expiry or revocation if read access remains valid, but cannot create a new transfer. Baseline B performs the same fresh authorization and balanced posting for each executed attempt, ignoring D. In both arms acknowledgment generation follows durable commitment; losing an acknowledgment never rolls back commitment. Settlement is an idempotent txid-based status transition held fixed between arms.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Bounded retry, delayed responses, and settlement closure
reasoning_steps.argument: Fix an agent deadline D_agent, grant expiry E>D_agent, maximum retries R, timeout/backoff schedule, and total call/time/token/monetary ceilings. At most R+1 write attempts may be sent, all before D_agent; reads and reconciliation also consume prespecified budgets. Timeouts mean UNKNOWN, not FAILED or CANCELED. A delayed original request may execute after a retry or after client stopping. A matching committed receipt delivered before D_agent permits final output; subsequent responses cannot trigger a new operation or reset the retry count. A delayed response alone never changes ledger state. At exhaustion the client outputs UNKNOWN/ESCALATE, not success. Choose settlement horizon H>E+s, where each committed transaction settles within s in the core contract. At H, Q=1 means all run transactions are settled and every queued or future old-grant request is permanently unable to create another economic effect. Commit-time expiry supplies this fence; a client stop does not. Fault tests may violate settlement progress, in which case Q can be zero.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Exact success, harmful-event, and safe-stop predicates
reasoning_steps.argument: Let L_H be all run-attributable economic commitments through H, including requests still executing after the client stops. Order them by authoritative commit sequence. A commitment is bad if it differs from fixture intent p*, was unauthorized at commitment, or is the second or later commitment for that one intended operation. A settlement event is bad if it settles a bad commitment or creates any extra economic posting. Let Harm_H indicate any bad commitment or settlement by H, and DelayedHarm_(D_agent,H] indicate any such bad event whose event time is in (D_agent,H]. Thus a correct first commitment after D_agent misses the deadline but is not automatically harm; a duplicate committed before D_agent and settled afterward is delayed harm under this event-based definition. Exact task success Y_H=1 iff: L_H contains exactly one commitment, it equals p* and was authorized, its commit time is at most D_agent, it is settled by H, no bad settlement occurred, Q=1, the client output by D_agent contains its matching txid/payload/committed receipt, and all client budget limits were respected. Otherwise Y_H=0. A safe omission stop requires an UNKNOWN/ESCALATE output, L_H empty, Q=1, and no harmful event; it is not task success. Missing audit data produce UNKNOWN labels, not invented zero harm or known success. These are horizon-specific predicates, not claims of lifetime safety.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Proof of the duplicate-commit exclusion
reasoning_steps.argument: Initially fix any K with D[K] absent. Induct over serialized server transitions. A rejection, replay, response event, or settlement creates no commitment. The first successful fresh execution inserts exactly one commitment and D[K] together. Thereafter every matching execution takes the replay branch and every mismatching execution takes the conflict branch. Crash recovery preserves both the commitment and D[K], so it cannot restore the absent-key state while retaining the effect. Therefore the commitment count for K is at most one for every finite history. Serialization handles simultaneous attempts; transport order and lost acknowledgments are irrelevant to this invariant. If K is initially occupied, no fresh commitment is possible under it. If every attempt for one operation uses the same K, that operation inherits the bound. A stable operation label without stable K does not establish the premise.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. What the invariant does not prove
reasoning_steps.argument: Zero commitments satisfies at-most-one. All requests can be dropped, authorization can expire, funds can be insufficient, a receipt can arrive too late, or settlement can fail. Conditional completion additionally follows only if an authorized matching execution linearizes before D_agent, its receipt is delivered and correctly output before D_agent within budget, settlement and closure hold by H, and no other faulty path changes the ledger. Then the invariant supplies uniqueness and these additional conditions supply every remaining clause of Y_H. This is not an eventual-delivery guarantee under bounded retries. Wrong fixture intent, a compromised authorizer, a separate non-deduplicated downstream effect, and writes under fresh keys remain outside the invariant. Atomic idempotency also does not undo a first incorrect authorized transfer.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Concrete paired trace conventions
reasoning_steps.argument: For the truth table use D_agent=10, E=12, H=15, s<=2, R=1, sends at times 0 and, if no valid receipt has arrived, 4; the timeout occurs at 3. Accounts contain enough funds for both baseline attempts. Ordinary commitments occur at 1 or 5, settle one unit later, and delivered receipts arrive before 10 unless specified. Both arms receive the same attempt-indexed fault schedule and isolated initial state. A replay produces no settlement event because it creates no transaction. The tuple is (n_D,n_H,r,q,y,d): commitment counts by 10 and 15, whether a matching receipt was output by 10, closure Q, success Y_H, and DelayedHarm_(10,15]. A valid local receipt does not certify uniqueness: r may be 1 when y is 0. All entries are deductions from specified traces, not observations. The table is a set of discriminating witnesses, not exhaustive state-space verification.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Contract-breaking and added-dependency controls
reasoning_steps.argument:
Using the same tuple and default timing:
Control | B | A | interpretation
Lost first acknowledgment; client regenerates K for retry | (2,2,1,1,0,0) | (2,2,1,1,0,0) | stable-key premise broken
Retry commits at 5; its D record is wrongly deleted at 9; queued original executes at 11 | (1,2,1,1,0,1) | (1,2,1,1,0,1) | retention premise broken
First economic write at 1 survives crash but its D record does not; retry at 5 | (2,2,1,1,0,0) | (2,2,1,1,0,0) | atomic durability premise broken

These controls intentionally change assumptions or inject a mechanism-specific fault. They are not admissible counterexamples to the proved invariant. Their frequencies and costs must be measured rather than chosen to favor either arm.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Key collision and recovery introduce different risks
reasoning_steps.argument: A separate two-operation regression test is necessary because the primary task requires only one operation. Give two valid grants for distinct operations p1 and p2, sufficient funds, timely receipts, and settlement. With distinct keys both arms have per-operation counts (1,1) and satisfy the two-operation rubric. If the client incorrectly assigns the same K to both, B still obtains (1,1), whereas correct A obtains (1,0): p2 is rejected as KEY_CONFLICT because operation identity is part of the payload. A's two-operation success is false, but duplicate/unauthorized harm is zero. If payload checking instead omits operation identity and silently returns p1's receipt for p2, that is an additional implementation defect; an oracle checking operation IDs rejects it. Conversely, changing K to escape a conflict after an ambiguous first commitment can create two effects for the first operation. Conflicts therefore require reconciliation or explicit escalation, not automatic new-key retry. Deduplication introduces storage, contention, access-control, retention, and reconciliation obligations; these can shift risk from duplication to omission or availability.

reasoning_steps.title: 13. Oracle audit and reproducible next test
reasoning_steps.argument: Implement the ledger and an independently written event-replay oracle from this specification. The oracle must compare exact fixture intent, append-only transaction multiplicities, commit-time authorization versions, both sides of each balanced posting, settlement records, queued-request fences, client output timestamps, and budget counters. Final net balances alone are insufficient because compensation or offsetting errors could hide duplicate effects. First test the listed paired schedules, then enumerate bounded interleavings around authorization, atomic persistence, acknowledgment, restart, settlement, expiry, and record retention. Independently check transaction counts against account deltas and deliberately corrupt logs/receipts to verify that missing or inconsistent evidence is not certified as success. Preserve raw events, fixture versions, fault schedules, and arm configuration. Such finite tests would assess implementation fidelity, not prove the general invariant or establish population benefit. Later repeated independent task clusters should report success, total and delayed harm, safe stops, latency, calls, and cost with uncertainty; the previous comparison bound requires separately justified oracle-error allowances.

Their originals were not supplied. Operational failure ada09312-ae3f-43ea-a461-b2a04b05f66b is not evidence against the mathematics and is not retried. The contribution is a proposed auditable mechanism specification using standard transaction reasoning. Material novelty relative to literature, real-tool contract compliance, practical overhead, empirical generality, and effects on open-ended agent tasks are not assessed.

artifacts.strategy_title: Develop a rigorous framework for measuring AI agent reliability
artifacts.claim_or_question: A stratified, paired comparison can certify a positive reliability difference without assuming independent judge errors or independent repeated runs. For each stratum h, let C_A indicate joint automated/reference acceptance of system A, and D_B indicate joint automated/reference rejection of baseline B. Assume Pr(C_A=1,Y_A=0|h)≤η_Ah and Pr(D_B=1,Y_B=1|h)≤η_Bh, where Y denotes actual success. With fixed population weights w_h, n_h independent paired task clusters per stratum, arbitrary dependence within clusters, and the cluster score Z_hi equal to the mean of C_A+D_B−1 over scheduled run pairs, define S=Σ_h w_h²/n_h and E=Σ_h w_h(η_Ah+η_Bh). Then L=max{−1, Σ_h w_h mean_i(Z_hi)−E−sqrt[2S log(1/α)]} is a one-sided (1−α) lower confidence bound on p_A−p_B. Conservative missing-data scores may replace Z_hi as specified below. Thus L>0 supports improvement only for the fixed target distribution, protocol, budgets, and truth-error allowances.

investigator_output.claim: A stratified, paired comparison can certify a positive reliability difference without assuming independent judge errors or independent repeated runs. For each stratum h, let C_A indicate joint automated/reference acceptance of system A, and D_B indicate joint automated/reference rejection of baseline B. Assume Pr(C_A=1,Y_A=0|h)≤η_Ah and Pr(D_B=1,Y_B=1|h)≤η_Bh, where Y denotes actual success. With fixed population weights w_h, n_h independent paired task clusters per stratum, arbitrary dependence within clusters, and the cluster score Z_hi equal to the mean of C_A+D_B−1 over scheduled run pairs, define S=Σ_h w_h²/n_h and E=Σ_h w_h(η_Ah+η_Bh). Then L=max{−1, Σ_h w_h mean_i(Z_hi)−E−sqrt[2S log(1/α)]} is a one-sided (1−α) lower confidence bound on p_A−p_B. Conservative missing-data scores may replace Z_hi as specified below. Thus L>0 supports improvement only for the fixed target distribution, protocol, budgets, and truth-error allowances.
investigator_output.method: Develop a standalone conditional lemma addressing the ledger's stratification, paired-comparison, and missingness obligations. The hypothesis is that improvement certification requires a lower bound for A and an upper bound for B, not two lower bounds. The discriminating analytical outcomes are an explicit baseline false-rejection allowance, a cluster-level weighted confidence bound, and a counterexample to subtracting lower bounds. The supplied extract of artifact 0310e2ff-4aa0-4c95-b1a8-795559e484b8 motivates the extension, but the argument is rederived here rather than treating its prior assertions as certified premises. reasoning_steps.title: 1. Define the target population and paired sampling unit
reasoning_steps.argument: Fix H task strata, distributions D_h, weights w_h≥0 summing to one, positive integer cluster counts n_h for positive-weight strata, and positive integer run counts r_h. For system s∈{A,B}, define p_sh as the probability of actual rubric satisfaction when a task is drawn from D_h and a run is selected uniformly from its scheduled r_h-run batch. The target contrast is Δ=Σ_h w_h(p_Ah−p_Bh). Each cluster contains both systems' batches on the same sampled task. Clusters are independent across all h,i and identically distributed within each stratum. Dependence among all runs, systems, and judges inside a cluster is unrestricted.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Fix controls and prevent interference
reasoning_steps.argument: Fix versions, prompts, success rubrics, observation horizons, tools, retry policies, and compute/time/monetary caps before outcomes. Evaluate both systems from equivalent isolated environment snapshots; randomize execution order where order could matter, without allowing one system to alter the other's state. Count safeguards, verification, and recovery against each system's stated execution budget. Equal caps define the primary budget-matched contrast; unequal budgets define a different contrast and must be labeled accordingly. Identical task distributions and isolated execution make the paired marginals match the target estimand. These are requirements for an implementation, not properties established for an actual benchmark.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. State directional truth-error allowances
reasoning_steps.argument: For each run, O_s∈{0,1} is automated acceptance, R_s∈{0,1} is reference certification, and Y_s∈{0,1} is actual success. Set C_A=1{O_A=1,R_A=1} and D_B=1{O_B=0,R_B=0}. Under uniform run selection within stratum h, assume e_Ah=Pr(C_A=1,Y_A=0|h)≤η_Ah and e_Bh=Pr(D_B=1,Y_B=1|h)≤η_Bh. These are unconditional error probabilities within the stratum, not conditional error rates among accepted or rejected cases. The second allowance is new relative to a one-system lower-bound construction: jointly rejected B executions can nevertheless be genuine successes. Neither allowance follows from agreement between the judges.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Derive the population lower contrast
reasoning_steps.argument: Pointwise, Y_A≥C_A−C_A(1−Y_A). Also 1−Y_B≥D_B−D_BY_B, hence Y_B≤1−D_B+D_BY_B. Subtracting and taking stratum expectations gives p_Ah−p_Bh≥E[C_A+D_B−1|h]−e_Ah−e_Bh. Weighting and applying the allowances yields Δ≥μ−E, where μ=Σ_h w_h E[C_A+D_B−1|h] and E=Σ_h w_h(η_Ah+η_Bh). No independence of truth, automated judgments, reference judgments, or the two systems is used in these inequalities.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Explain the baseline upper-bound requirement
reasoning_steps.argument: The same derivation gives p_Bh≤min{1,1−Pr(D_B=1|h)+η_Bh}. A restriction only on jointly accepted failures leaves Y_B=1 everywhere observationally possible: that assignment creates no accepted failures. Consequently such a restriction alone supplies no nontrivial baseline upper bound. Likewise, p_A≥L_A and p_B≥L_B do not imply Δ≥L_A−L_B. For example, L_A=0.8, L_B=0.7, p_A=0.8, and p_B=1 satisfy both lower bounds, but Δ=−0.2 rather than the purported lower bound 0.1. This is an analytical counterexample, not a measured agent result.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Reduce dependent runs to bounded cluster scores
reasoning_steps.argument: For task cluster i in stratum h, let Z_hi=(1/r_h)Σ_j(C_Ahij+D_Bhij−1). Every Z_hi lies in [−1,1], and E[Z_hi]=E[C_A+D_B−1|h] by the definition of uniform run selection. Thus μ̂=Σ_h(w_h/n_h)Σ_i Z_hi has expectation μ. Only the cluster scores need be independent. Increasing r_h does not increase the number of independent task units, and no factor r_h enters the worst-case concentration guarantee. Pairing may reduce actual variability, but this range-based bound does not assume or guarantee a variance reduction.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Establish the finite-sample confidence guarantee
reasoning_steps.argument: For each independent weighted summand (w_h/n_h)Z_hi, the range length is 2w_h/n_h. The bounded-variable exponential-moment inequality gives E exp[λ(μ̂−μ)]≤exp(λ²S/2), with S=Σ_h w_h²/n_h. Markov's inequality followed by minimization over λ>0 yields Pr(μ̂−μ≥t)≤exp[−t²/(2S)]. Taking t=sqrt[2S log(1/α)] gives μ≥μ̂−t with probability at least 1−α. Combining with step 4 proves Δ≥μ̂−t−E on this event. Since Δ≥−1 always, clipping the lower endpoint at −1 preserves coverage. This is the standard bounded-sum concentration method applied to independent tasks, not run-level binomial analysis.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Handle missing labels and scheduled attempts conservatively
reasoning_steps.argument: Retain a preregistered roster of all sampled task clusters and scheduled run slots; never divide only by completed runs. Record C_A as 1 only when both acceptance labels are available and equal 1, otherwise use 0. Record D_B as 1 only when both rejection labels are available and equal 0, otherwise use 0. These replacements are pointwise no larger than the corresponding complete-data indicators, so the resulting score Z̃_hi≤Z_hi. A wholly missing pair receives −1. Therefore μ̂_obs≤μ̂ for every realized missingness pattern, and the same lower confidence formula remains conservative, even when missingness depends on outcomes. For missing attempts this argument requires well-defined full scheduled-execution outcomes and no interference from omission with other clusters. A known protocol crash can instead be labeled directly according to the rubric. If omitted tasks cannot be enumerated, or cancellation changes other executions' distributions, this argument does not apply; the target population or design must be repaired.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Allocate error across calibration, outcomes, and monitoring
reasoning_steps.argument: The stated 1−α guarantee treats η_Ah and η_Bh as valid fixed population bounds. If calibration instead supplies simultaneous upper allowances with failure probability at most β, the evaluation failure probability is at most α_eval+β by a union bound; independence between calibration and evaluation is unnecessary for this union bound, though each component guarantee still needs justification. For prespecified binary metrics k and deterministic analysis looks ℓ, allocate α_kℓ>0 with Σ_k,ℓ α_kℓ+β≤α_total and apply the theorem separately at each look using its fixed sample counts. A union bound then gives simultaneous coverage, permitting selection of a reporting or stopping look from that schedule. This does not justify unplanned metric selection, adaptive task sampling, changing protocols, or arbitrary continuous monitoring.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Check boundary cases and interpretation
reasoning_steps.argument: With H=1 and r=1 the result reduces to a paired bounded-score comparison. Zero-weight strata contribute nothing; a positive-weight stratum with no sampled clusters cannot use the displayed formula and must instead receive its trivial contrast lower bound −1 or be sampled. If all observations are missing, every observed score is −1 and clipping returns −1, certifying nothing. With perfect judges C_A=Y_A and D_B=1−Y_B, both allowances can be zero and Z is the actual paired success difference. Under arbitrary within-task dependence, identical repeated runs do not tighten the radius. A positive endpoint supports a fixed-protocol success advantage, not automatically a causal architectural benefit or a safety guarantee.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Specify a discriminating implementation test
reasoning_steps.argument: When execution is available, generate two-stratum finite-support task populations with exactly calculable Δ, e_Ah, and e_Bh. Vary n_h, r_h, stratum weights, within-task dependence from independent to identical runs, and shared judge errors. Include outcome-dependent label deletion while retaining every scheduled slot. Across independent panels, measure noncoverage of the stated endpoint and compare it with an intentionally naive run-independent analysis. Include violated-allowance and cross-cluster shared-state controls, which are outside the theorem. Report Monte Carlo uncertainty and endpoint width; finite coverage agreement tests implementation and these specified populations, not universal validity. This experiment has not been executed.

reasoning_assessments.rationale: Uniform selection from a fixed scheduled batch defines each marginal reliability, and fixed population weights define the contrast. Independence is imposed on paired task clusters, not their constituent runs. These are explicit premises of the conditional claim.

Fixed versions, policies, caps, and isolated snapshots define a coherent budget-matched comparison. Counting verification and recovery in the budget avoids an unreported resource advantage. The step correctly presents these controls as implementation requirements rather than established facts.

The two unconditional stratum error probabilities cover exactly the adverse directions needed for a lower contrast bound. They do not require independent judges. Acceptance is solely as explicit assumptions; the historical comparison is not needed for the mathematics.
C_A−C_A(1−Y_A)=C_AY_A≤Y_A, while D_B−D_BY_B=D_B(1−Y_B)≤1−Y_B. Subtraction, expectation, and nonnegative weighting therefore give Δ≥μ−E without judge or system independence.

The bound on jointly rejected genuine successes gives the stated upper bound for B. A bound only on accepted failures permits universal baseline success. The numerical example satisfies both proposed lower bounds but violates their purported contrast, decisively rejecting that subtraction rule.

A batch average of scores in [−1,1] remains in that interval. Its expectation equals the uniformly selected run-pair expectation even without exchangeability or independent runs. Consequently r_h provides no additional independent units for this range-based guarantee.

Summing squared weighted range lengths gives 4Σ_h w_h²/n_h=4S. The bounded-sum exponential-moment bound is therefore exp(λ²S/2), whose optimized upper tail is exp(−t²/(2S)). Combining that event with the population inequality and clipping at −1 preserves coverage.

Replacing an uncertified acceptance or rejection indicator by zero can only decrease C_A+D_B−1. Thus the observed endpoint cannot exceed the complete-data endpoint for any deletion pattern; no missing-at-random premise is needed. The stated full-roster and well-defined-outcome restrictions are essential.

Applying the fixed-sample guarantee to each prespecified metric and deterministic look supports scheduled stopping or reporting. The stated reductions follow directly from the formula. All-missing observations give −1 after clipping, and perfect judges recover actual paired success differences. An unsampled positive-weight stratum requires a separately combined trivial contribution, not division by zero. The interpretation correctly excludes automatic safety or architectural causality claims.

Known-truth finite-support populations permit independent calculation of the target and error allowances. reasoning_steps.title: 1. Define the target population and paired sampling unit
reasoning_steps.argument: Fix H task strata, distributions D_h, weights w_h≥0 summing to one, positive integer cluster counts n_h for positive-weight strata, and positive integer run counts r_h. For system s∈{A,B}, define p_sh as the probability of actual rubric satisfaction when a task is drawn from D_h and a run is selected uniformly from its scheduled r_h-run batch. The target contrast is Δ=Σ_h w_h(p_Ah−p_Bh). Each cluster contains both systems' batches on the same sampled task. Clusters are independent across all h,i and identically distributed within each stratum. Dependence among all runs, systems, and judges inside a cluster is unrestricted.

review.rationale: Uniform selection from a fixed scheduled batch defines each marginal reliability, and fixed population weights define the contrast. Independence is imposed on paired task clusters, not their constituent runs. These are explicit premises of the conditional claim.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Fix controls and prevent interference
reasoning_steps.argument: Fix versions, prompts, success rubrics, observation horizons, tools, retry policies, and compute/time/monetary caps before outcomes. Evaluate both systems from equivalent isolated environment snapshots; randomize execution order where order could matter, without allowing one system to alter the other's state. Count safeguards, verification, and recovery against each system's stated execution budget. Equal caps define the primary budget-matched contrast; unequal budgets define a different contrast and must be labeled accordingly. Identical task distributions and isolated execution make the paired marginals match the target estimand. These are requirements for an implementation, not properties established for an actual benchmark.

review.rationale: Fixed versions, policies, caps, and isolated snapshots define a coherent budget-matched comparison. Counting verification and recovery in the budget avoids an unreported resource advantage. The step correctly presents these controls as implementation requirements rather than established facts.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. State directional truth-error allowances
reasoning_steps.argument: For each run, O_s∈{0,1} is automated acceptance, R_s∈{0,1} is reference certification, and Y_s∈{0,1} is actual success. Set C_A=1{O_A=1,R_A=1} and D_B=1{O_B=0,R_B=0}. Under uniform run selection within stratum h, assume e_Ah=Pr(C_A=1,Y_A=0|h)≤η_Ah and e_Bh=Pr(D_B=1,Y_B=1|h)≤η_Bh. These are unconditional error probabilities within the stratum, not conditional error rates among accepted or rejected cases. The second allowance is new relative to a one-system lower-bound construction: jointly rejected B executions can nevertheless be genuine successes. Neither allowance follows from agreement between the judges.

review.rationale: The two unconditional stratum error probabilities cover exactly the adverse directions needed for a lower contrast bound. They do not require independent judges. Acceptance is solely as explicit assumptions; the historical comparison is not needed for the mathematics.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Derive the population lower contrast
reasoning_steps.argument: Pointwise, Y_A≥C_A−C_A(1−Y_A). Also 1−Y_B≥D_B−D_BY_B, hence Y_B≤1−D_B+D_BY_B. Subtracting and taking stratum expectations gives p_Ah−p_Bh≥E[C_A+D_B−1|h]−e_Ah−e_Bh. Weighting and applying the allowances yields Δ≥μ−E, where μ=Σ_h w_h E[C_A+D_B−1|h] and E=Σ_h w_h(η_Ah+η_Bh). No independence of truth, automated judgments, reference judgments, or the two systems is used in these inequalities.

review.rationale: C_A−C_A(1−Y_A)=C_AY_A≤Y_A, while D_B−D_BY_B=D_B(1−Y_B)≤1−Y_B. Subtraction, expectation, and nonnegative weighting therefore give Δ≥μ−E without judge or system independence.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Explain the baseline upper-bound requirement
reasoning_steps.argument: The same derivation gives p_Bh≤min{1,1−Pr(D_B=1|h)+η_Bh}. A restriction only on jointly accepted failures leaves Y_B=1 everywhere observationally possible: that assignment creates no accepted failures. Consequently such a restriction alone supplies no nontrivial baseline upper bound. Likewise, p_A≥L_A and p_B≥L_B do not imply Δ≥L_A−L_B. For example, L_A=0.8, L_B=0.7, p_A=0.8, and p_B=1 satisfy both lower bounds, but Δ=−0.2 rather than the purported lower bound 0.1. This is an analytical counterexample, not a measured agent result.

review.rationale: The bound on jointly rejected genuine successes gives the stated upper bound for B. A bound only on accepted failures permits universal baseline success. The numerical example satisfies both proposed lower bounds but violates their purported contrast, decisively rejecting that subtraction rule.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Reduce dependent runs to bounded cluster scores
reasoning_steps.argument: For task cluster i in stratum h, let Z_hi=(1/r_h)Σ_j(C_Ahij+D_Bhij−1). Every Z_hi lies in [−1,1], and E[Z_hi]=E[C_A+D_B−1|h] by the definition of uniform run selection. Pairing may reduce actual variability, but this range-based bound does not assume or guarantee a variance reduction.

review.rationale: A batch average of scores in [−1,1] remains in that interval. Its expectation equals the uniformly selected run-pair expectation even without exchangeability or independent runs. Consequently r_h provides no additional independent units for this range-based guarantee.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Establish the finite-sample confidence guarantee
reasoning_steps.argument: For each independent weighted summand (w_h/n_h)Z_hi, the range length is 2w_h/n_h. The bounded-variable exponential-moment inequality gives E exp[λ(μ̂−μ)]≤exp(λ²S/2), with S=Σ_h w_h²/n_h. Markov's inequality followed by minimization over λ>0 yields Pr(μ̂−μ≥t)≤exp[−t²/(2S)]. review.rationale: Summing squared weighted range lengths gives 4Σ_h w_h²/n_h=4S. The bounded-sum exponential-moment bound is therefore exp(λ²S/2), whose optimized upper tail is exp(−t²/(2S)). Combining that event with the population inequality and clipping at −1 preserves coverage.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Handle missing labels and scheduled attempts conservatively
reasoning_steps.argument: Retain a preregistered roster of all sampled task clusters and scheduled run slots; never divide only by completed runs. Record C_A as 1 only when both acceptance labels are available and equal 1, otherwise use 0. Record D_B as 1 only when both rejection labels are available and equal 0, otherwise use 0. These replacements are pointwise no larger than the corresponding complete-data indicators, so the resulting score Z̃_hi≤Z_hi. A wholly missing pair receives −1. Therefore μ̂_obs≤μ̂ for every realized missingness pattern, and the same lower confidence formula remains conservative, even when missingness depends on outcomes. For missing attempts this argument requires well-defined full scheduled-execution outcomes and no interference from omission with other clusters. A known protocol crash can instead be labeled directly according to the rubric. If omitted tasks cannot be enumerated, or cancellation changes other executions' distributions, this argument does not apply; the target population or design must be repaired.

review.rationale: Replacing an uncertified acceptance or rejection indicator by zero can only decrease C_A+D_B−1. The stated full-roster and well-defined-outcome restrictions are essential.

reasoning_steps.argument: The stated 1−α guarantee treats η_Ah and η_Bh as valid fixed population bounds. Applying the fixed-sample guarantee to each prespecified metric and deterministic look supports scheduled stopping or reporting. reasoning_steps.title: Define the workflow and recovery requirement
reasoning_steps.argument: A task requires exactly one irreversible external effect, such as appending one uniquely identifiable but non-deduplicated transaction to a write-only service. The agent records a local pending operation, sends it, and expects an acknowledgment. Let C be the number of committed effects for that logical operation. At a prespecified deadline H, success requires C=1 and a truthful terminal report. C=0 is incomplete; C>=2 is duplication. Safe escalation is recorded separately and is not successful completion. The impossibility argument uses only the necessary condition C=1, so adding report correctness cannot weaken it.

reasoning_steps.title: Construct two observationally identical histories
reasoning_steps.argument: In history W0, the original request is dropped before committing, leaving C=0. In W1, it commits once but its acknowledgment is lost, leaving C=1. A crash then restores the same local pending checkpoint in both histories. The service exposes no status query, durable deduplication, compensating operation, or other distinguishing observation before the first possible retry or deadline. Thus the local transcript and all information available for that decision are identical. This construction does not apply if an authoritative receipt or another informative observation is available.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive the randomized lower bound
reasoning_steps.argument: Let q be the probability that the policy issues at least one retry before H. Because the two histories are indistinguishable until that decision, q is the same in both. Assume every issued retry commits at least once before H, and committed effects cannot be removed. In W0, success requires a retry, so Pr(success|W0)<=q. In W1, any retry creates duplication, so Pr(success|W1)<=1-q. Therefore min{Pr(success|W0),Pr(success|W1)}<=min(q,1-q)<=1/2. Equivalently, worst-case failure probability is at least 1/2. Additional retries or false completion reports can only reduce success. Under an equal mixture of W0 and W1, average success is also at most 1/2. These are bounds for the constructed histories, not population estimates.

reasoning_steps.title: Check tightness, deterministic policies, and termination
reasoning_steps.argument: Within this construction, a fair coin that chooses between one retry and no retry achieves external-state correctness probability 1/2 in each history when the chosen retry commits exactly once. Thus the external-effect bound is tight, although truthful completion may require more information. A deterministic retry duplicates W1; a deterministic stop leaves W0 incomplete. Waiting forever does not satisfy the finite deadline. Safe stopping can guarantee no additional duplicate but cannot guarantee task completion. If retry delivery is not assured, the upper bounds still hold, but the tightness example need not.

reasoning_steps.title: Identify the propagation path and the boundary of local recovery
reasoning_steps.argument: The causal chain is ambiguous transport outcome -> divergent external state hidden behind the same local pending state -> retry duplicates an already committed effect, or stopping omits an uncommitted effect -> later workflow steps consume an incorrect effect count. Replaying the checkpoint, compressing memory differently, changing the plan, or replacing the model supplies no new information about which history occurred. Such changes therefore cannot evade the bound while the information and action assumptions remain unchanged. Rolling back local memory does not roll back the external effect. An independent status observation or a different service contract changes the assumptions and can change recoverability.

reasoning_steps.title: Give a sufficient service contract that changes the scope
reasoning_steps.argument: Suppose the agent durably stores a logical-operation key k and payload x before sending. The service maintains a durable record M[k] and atomically couples the external effect with installing its receipt in M[k]. A call with a new key performs the effect and records the receipt atomically; a repeated call with the same key and payload returns that receipt without another effect; a payload mismatch is rejected. Atomic serialization implies at most one effect for k: only the first absent-to-present transition can create it. If no effect has occurred, a delivered call can create it; if it has occurred, a delivered retry returns its receipt. Under eventual successful delivery and service progress, retrying the same stored key therefore yields exactly one effect and a receipt. This is a conditional sufficiency argument, not a claim that existing tools implement this contract.

reasoning_steps.title: State the remaining boundaries of that contract
reasoning_steps.argument: The contract fails to establish exactly-once behavior if recovery generates a fresh key, keys collide across logical operations, records expire before retries, or recording the receipt and performing the effect are separate crashable operations. For example, committing an effect and then crashing before recording M[k] recreates the original ambiguity. Eventual delivery gives eventual completion, not a finite-H guarantee. Per-operation deduplication also does not prove that the payload was correct, that a multi-service workflow is atomic, or that delayed external consequences are harmless.

reasoning_steps.title: Specify a falsifiable fault-injection test
reasoning_steps.argument: Use a synthetic append service with a hidden audit ledger as the ground-truth oracle. Fork identical pending checkpoints into W0 and W1. Compare always-retry, checkpoint restart without deduplication, safe escalation, and stable-key retry against an atomic deduplicating service. Include normal acknowledgment and permanently unavailable-service controls. Fix task payloads, model/prompt/tool versions, retry limits, H, and total budgets; randomize policy assignment and execution order across isolated task instances. Audit effect counts, terminal-report truth, unrelated-state changes, time to detection, escalation, calls, latency, and cost. The discriminating outcome is duplication in W1 or omission in W0 for local-only recovery, versus one effect after delivered stable-key retries under the specified contract. A policy apparently exceeding the bound requires inspecting whether it received distinguishing information or violated another construction assumption. Treat paired histories from one task as a cluster, retain all attempted runs, and report oracle-unavailable runs conservatively as uncertified rather than dropping them. Repeat across independent tasks and prespecified seeds; larger samples assess variability, not the universal theorem. This experiment is proposed, not executed.

objective_review.claim: Conditional on: The task requires exactly one irreversible non-idempotent external effect by a fixed deadline; omission, duplication, and safe escalation are distinguished; The original request can be lost before commitment or committed with its acknowledgment lost, producing identical agent-visible pending checkpoints; No authoritative status observation, deduplication mechanism, or compensation distinguishes the two histories before the first retry decision or deadline; Every issued retry in the constructed histories commits at least once before the deadline, and effects cannot subsequently be removed; Policy randomness has the same distribution in both histories and is not correlated with the hidden initial commitment; The separate sufficient-contract result assumes a durable pre-send key and payload, atomic effect-plus-receipt recording, persistent deduplication records, payload checking, and eventual delivery and service progress. objective_review.argument_summary: In cycle 1, steps 1–3, the same information forces the same retry probability q in W0 and W1. Success in W0 requires retry, while success in W1 requires no retry; their success probabilities are therefore bounded by q and 1-q. Step 4 supplies tightness for external-effect correctness when one retry commits exactly once, but its relaxation of delivery assurance is unsupported. Steps 5–7 explain why local recovery cannot repair hidden external divergence and why atomic per-key effect/receipt recording changes the problem. Step 8 is a proposed discriminating experiment, not measured evidence.

argument_steps.title: Define the workflow and recovery requirement
argument_steps.argument: A task requires exactly one irreversible external effect, such as appending one uniquely identifiable but non-deduplicated transaction to a write-only service. The agent records a local pending operation, sends it, and expects an acknowledgment. Let C be the number of committed effects for that logical operation. At a prespecified deadline H, success requires C=1 and a truthful terminal report. C=0 is incomplete; C>=2 is duplication. Safe escalation is recorded separately and is not successful completion. The impossibility argument uses only the necessary condition C=1, so adding report correctness cannot weaken it.

review.rationale: The fixed-deadline rubric separates omission, duplication, reporting, and escalation. Since C=1 is necessary for full success, an upper bound on external-effect correctness also bounds full task success. These are explicit premises of the conditional claim.

argument_steps.title: Construct two observationally identical histories
argument_steps.argument: In history W0, the original request is dropped before committing, leaving C=0. In W1, it commits once but its acknowledgment is lost, leaving C=1. A crash then restores the same local pending checkpoint in both histories. The service exposes no status query, durable deduplication, compensating operation, or other distinguishing observation before the first possible retry or deadline. Thus the local transcript and all information available for that decision are identical. This construction does not apply if an authoritative receipt or another informative observation is available.

review.rationale: Dropping the request before commitment and dropping its acknowledgment after commitment can leave the same pending checkpoint with different external counts. The explicit exclusion of distinguishing observations makes the decision information identical; this is a constructed premise, not an observed property of tools.

argument_steps.title: Derive the randomized lower bound
argument_steps.argument: Let q be the probability that the policy issues at least one retry before H. Because the two histories are indistinguishable until that decision, q is the same in both. Assume every issued retry commits at least once before H, and committed effects cannot be removed. In W0, success requires a retry, so Pr(success|W0)<=q. In W1, any retry creates duplication, so Pr(success|W1)<=1-q. Therefore min{Pr(success|W0),Pr(success|W1)}<=min(q,1-q)<=1/2. Equivalently, worst-case failure probability is at least 1/2. Additional retries or false completion reports can only reduce success. Under an equal mixture of W0 and W1, average success is also at most 1/2. These are bounds for the constructed histories, not population estimates.

review.rationale: Identical information and hidden-state-independent randomness give the same probability q of issuing a first retry. Under guaranteed retry commitment, W0 success implies retry and W1 success implies no retry. Thus the two upper bounds, their worst-case consequence, and the equal-mixture upper bound follow without estimating any deployment frequency.

argument_steps.title: Check tightness, deterministic policies, and termination
argument_steps.argument: Within this construction, a fair coin that chooses between one retry and no retry achieves external-state correctness probability 1/2 in each history when the chosen retry commits exactly once. Thus the external-effect bound is tight, although truthful completion may require more information. A deterministic retry duplicates W1; a deterministic stop leaves W0 incomplete. Waiting forever does not satisfy the finite deadline. Safe stopping can guarantee no additional duplicate but cannot guarantee task completion. If retry delivery is not assured, the upper bounds still hold, but the tightness example need not.

review.rationale: The fair-coin example establishes tightness for external-effect correctness under exactly one commitment per chosen retry. The deterministic-policy and finite-deadline observations also follow. The final delivery-relaxation sentence does not follow.
review.objection: If retries can fail to commit, issuing a retry need not duplicate W1, so Pr(success|W1) <= 1-q is no longer valid. Always retrying with all retries dropped gives q=1 while W1 remains externally correct. Retain the original delivery premise, or formulate a new bound with additional coupling and observation restrictions.

argument_steps.title: Identify the propagation path and the boundary of local recovery
argument_steps.argument: The causal chain is ambiguous transport outcome -> divergent external state hidden behind the same local pending state -> retry duplicates an already committed effect, or stopping omits an uncommitted effect -> later workflow steps consume an incorrect effect count. Replaying the checkpoint, compressing memory differently, changing the plan, or replacing the model supplies no new information about which history occurred. Such changes therefore cannot evade the bound while the information and action assumptions remain unchanged. Rolling back local memory does not roll back the external effect. An independent status observation or a different service contract changes the assumptions and can change recoverability.

review.rationale: Local replay, replanning, or model replacement cannot distinguish the constructed histories when they preserve the same information and action restrictions. Local rollback does not remove irreversible service effects. The proposed later propagation is a possible workflow consequence, not a measured prevalence claim.

argument_steps.title: Give a sufficient service contract that changes the scope
argument_steps.argument: Suppose the agent durably stores a logical-operation key k and payload x before sending. The service maintains a durable record M[k] and atomically couples the external effect with installing its receipt in M[k]. A call with a new key performs the effect and records the receipt atomically; a repeated call with the same key and payload returns that receipt without another effect; a payload mismatch is rejected. Atomic serialization implies at most one effect for k: only the first absent-to-present transition can create it. If no effect has occurred, a delivered call can create it; if it has occurred, a delivered retry returns its receipt. Under eventual successful delivery and service progress, retrying the same stored key therefore yields exactly one effect and a receipt. This is a conditional sufficiency argument, not a claim that existing tools implement this contract.

review.rationale: With durable per-operation state and atomic serialization, only one absent-to-present key transition can create an effect; subsequent identical calls return the recorded receipt. Eventual successful delivery and progress yield an effect and receipt, but do not imply completion by H. This argument is conditional on the stipulated service semantics, not evidence that a real service implements them.

argument_steps.title: State the remaining boundaries of that contract
argument_steps.argument: The contract fails to establish exactly-once behavior if recovery generates a fresh key, keys collide across logical operations, records expire before retries, or recording the receipt and performing the effect are separate crashable operations. For example, committing an effect and then crashing before recording M[k] recreates the original ambiguity. Eventual delivery gives eventual completion, not a finite-H guarantee. Per-operation deduplication also does not prove that the payload was correct, that a multi-service workflow is atomic, or that delayed external consequences are harmless.

review.rationale: Fresh keys, collisions, expiry, and non-atomic effect/receipt writes remove premises used by the per-key invariant. The effect-before-receipt crash trace specifically permits duplication on retry. Per-operation uniqueness does not establish payload correctness, cross-service atomicity, or absence of delayed harm.

reasoning_steps.title: Define the population, pairing, and estimand
reasoning_steps.argument: Choose finitely many strata h=1,...,H, with fixed target-population weights w_h≥0 summing to one. In each positive-weight stratum sample n_h≥1 independent task clusters. For each task, execute systems A and B in isolated copies of the same initial environment, using a fixed number r_h≥1 of scheduled runs per system. Within-cluster run dependence and dependence between systems are unrestricted. Let Y_shij be actual binary rubric satisfaction and S_shij=O_shij R_shij be joint automated acceptance and reference certification, for system s, cluster i, and run j. Define p_sh as the expectation of the cluster-average Y and p_s=Σ_h w_h p_sh. Thus the target is a weighted task distribution followed by uniform selection among scheduled runs, not a run-count-weighted mixture of tasks.

reasoning_steps.title: State the asymmetric truth-error allowances
reasoning_steps.argument: For a uniformly selected scheduled run in stratum h, assume Pr(S_A=1,Y_A=0)≤η_Ah and Pr(S_B=0,Y_B=1)≤ξ_Bh, with allowances in [0,1]. These are unconditional probabilities, not error rates conditional on certification. They need not be independent of agent behavior, each other, or task difficulty. The first controls intervention false certification; the second controls baseline true successes missed by certification. The earlier supplied extract discusses only a lower-bound-oriented allowance. The baseline missed-success allowance is an additional premise needed for this comparison, not something inferred from judge agreement.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive the population improvement inequality
reasoning_steps.argument: For binary Y and S, Y=S−1{S=1,Y=0}+1{S=0,Y=1}. Consequently E[Y_A]≥E[S_A]−η_Ah and E[Y_B]≤E[S_B]+ξ_Bh in stratum h. Subtracting the second inequality from the first gives Δ_h≥E[S_A−S_B]−η_Ah−ξ_Bh. Multiplying by nonnegative weights and summing yields Δ≥d−E_err, where d=Σ_h w_h E[S_A−S_B] and E_err=Σ_h w_h(η_Ah+ξ_Bh). Also Δ≥−1. No independence of the judges was used.

reasoning_steps.title: Explain why two reliability lower bounds cannot establish improvement
reasoning_steps.argument: Consider S_A=1 and S_B=0 on every execution, with Y_A=Y_B=1. Both systems have zero false certification. Their certification-based reliability lower bounds can be 1 and 0, yet their true improvement is zero, not one. Thus subtracting lower bounds can overstate improvement. In this example ξ_B=1, so the additional baseline allowance correctly removes the apparent improvement. This is an identification counterexample, not an observed agent result.

reasoning_steps.title: Concentrate independent task clusters rather than dependent runs
reasoning_steps.argument: Let X_hi=(1/r_h)Σ_j(S_Ahij−S_Bhij), so X_hi∈[−1,1], and D=Σ_h(w_h/n_h)Σ_i X_hi. Under independent clusters, E[D]=d. A centered variable supported on an interval of length 2 has moment-generating function at most exp(λ²/2). Applying this bound to the weighted independent X_hi gives E[exp(λ(D−d))]≤exp(λ²V/2), where V=Σ_h w_h²/n_h. Markov's inequality and minimization at λ=t/V give Pr(D−d≥t)≤exp(−t²/(2V)). Taking t=sqrt(2V log(1/α)) shows d≥D−t with probability at least 1−α. Repetition count r_h does not enter the worst-case radius: perfectly correlated repeats cannot create additional independent tasks.

reasoning_steps.title: Handle missing judgments conservatively without discarding tasks
reasoning_steps.argument: Define complete certification variables by the fixed judging protocol, whether or not each label is observed. For any missing S_A replace it by 0, and for any missing S_B replace it by 1; known labels remain unchanged. Let D_obs be the resulting weighted cluster difference. Pointwise D_obs≤D, even if missingness is outcome-dependent or correlated across tasks. Therefore the complete-data concentration event also implies d≥D_obs−t. This argument requires a well-defined complete protocol and scheduled denominators. It does not permit deleting missing tasks, silently treating missing truth labels as known, or applying complete-case analysis. A timeout is an actual failure only if the prespecified success rubric makes it one.

reasoning_steps.title: Combine the bounds and state coverage and edge cases
reasoning_steps.argument: On the event from the preceding steps, Δ≥D_obs−E_err−t and Δ≥−1, establishing the claimed L. For fixed valid allowances, coverage is at least 1−α. If allowances are instead simultaneous upper confidence bounds valid with probability at least 1−β, union bounding gives coverage at least 1−α−β, without requiring calibration and evaluation samples to be independent. Their statistical validity and target-population applicability still require justification. Zero-weight strata may be omitted; positive-weight unsampled strata are outside this theorem. With one cluster the bound remains valid but is usually uninformative. All missing labels give D_obs=−1 and hence L=−1. Multiple mechanisms, endpoints, or interim looks require additional prespecified error allocation; this fixed-comparison result does not cover unrestricted search.

reasoning_steps.title: Specify an architectural experiment that can use the guarantee
reasoning_steps.argument: Proposed task family: multi-step ledger workflows requiring exactly one authorized transfer, correct recipient and amount, and a reconciled receipt after a fixed settlement horizon. B uses a fixed bounded-retry policy; A uses the same policy with a stable task-scoped idempotency key and atomic server-side deduplication. Prespecify no-fault, timeout-before-commit, timeout-after-commit, and delayed-response strata and weights. Start each paired execution from an isolated identical snapshot, reset between scheduled runs, and randomize execution order. Hold model/prompt versions and hard token, tool-call, time, and monetary ceilings fixed, including safeguard overhead. The hypothesized benefit is fewer duplicate committed transfers after lost acknowledgments. Test regressions from accidental key reuse, incorrectly suppressed distinct operations, and exhausted budgets separately; these are proposed fault cases, not measured failures.

reasoning_steps.title: Connect observed outcomes to engineering claims without overclaiming
reasoning_steps.argument: In the proposed controlled environment, evaluate actual terminal ledger state and receipt consistency rather than agent completion claims. An exhaustive outcome oracle would permit η_Ah=ξ_Bh=0 only after its coverage of the declared success predicate is justified; being a separate program is insufficient. Keep delayed unauthorized effects, safe stops, retry counts, latency, and cost as separate prespecified outcomes rather than hiding them in binary success. Stable environment isolation and changing only idempotency handling would support attribution within this task protocol after data collection. Neither the guarantee nor the proposed design establishes benefit on open-ended tasks, shared production state, different budgets, or distribution shifts. The method uses standard bounded-variable concentration; literature novelty and empirical generality are not assessed.

reasoning_steps.title: Define the population, pairing, and estimand
reasoning_steps.argument: Choose finitely many strata h=1,...,H, with fixed target-population weights w_h≥0 summing to one. In each positive-weight stratum sample n_h≥1 independent task clusters. For each task, execute systems A and B in isolated copies of the same initial environment, using a fixed number r_h≥1 of scheduled runs per system. Within-cluster run dependence and dependence between systems are unrestricted. Let Y_shij be actual binary rubric satisfaction and S_shij=O_shij R_shij be joint automated acceptance and reference certification, for system s, cluster i, and run j. Define p_sh as the expectation of the cluster-average Y and p_s=Σ_h w_h p_sh. Thus the target is a weighted task distribution followed by uniform selection among scheduled runs, not a run-count-weighted mixture of tasks.

review.rationale: As a premise of the explicitly conditional claim, fixed strata and weights together with uniform selection among scheduled runs define a coherent task-weighted estimand. Isolated paired copies and unrestricted within-cluster dependence do not conflict with independence between complete task clusters.

reasoning_steps.title: State the asymmetric truth-error allowances
reasoning_steps.argument: For a uniformly selected scheduled run in stratum h, assume Pr(S_A=1,Y_A=0)≤η_Ah and Pr(S_B=0,Y_B=1)≤ξ_Bh, with allowances in [0,1]. These are unconditional probabilities, not error rates conditional on certification. They need not be independent of agent behavior, each other, or task difficulty. The first controls intervention false certification; the second controls baseline true successes missed by certification. The earlier supplied extract discusses only a lower-bound-oriented allowance. The baseline missed-success allowance is an additional premise needed for this comparison, not something inferred from judge agreement.

review.rationale: The listed assumptions explicitly include these unconditional directional error bounds. Intervention false certification can inflate intervention reliability, while baseline missed successes can depress baseline certification; these are the relevant adverse directions for a lower improvement bound. They are premises, not established calibration results. The supplied prior extract discusses only the lower-bound-oriented allowance.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive the population improvement inequality
reasoning_steps.argument: For binary Y and S, Y=S−1{S=1,Y=0}+1{S=0,Y=1}. Consequently E[Y_A]≥E[S_A]−η_Ah and E[Y_B]≤E[S_B]+ξ_Bh in stratum h. Subtracting the second inequality from the first gives Δ_h≥E[S_A−S_B]−η_Ah−ξ_Bh. Multiplying by nonnegative weights and summing yields Δ≥d−E_err, where d=Σ_h w_h E[S_A−S_B] and E_err=Σ_h w_h(η_Ah+ξ_Bh). Also Δ≥−1. No independence of the judges was used.

review.rationale: The binary identity is exact. Dropping intervention missed successes and baseline false certifications gives the stated lower and upper bounds respectively. Subtraction and nonnegative weighted summation preserve the inequality without judge independence.

reasoning_steps.title: Explain why two reliability lower bounds cannot establish improvement
reasoning_steps.argument: Consider S_A=1 and S_B=0 on every execution, with Y_A=Y_B=1. Both systems have zero false certification. Their certification-based reliability lower bounds can be 1 and 0, yet their true improvement is zero, not one. Thus subtracting lower bounds can overstate improvement. In this example ξ_B=1, so the additional baseline allowance correctly removes the apparent improvement. This is an identification counterexample, not an observed agent result.

review.rationale: With S_A=1, S_B=0, and both truth labels equal to one, the certification lower bounds differ by one while actual improvement is zero. Baseline missed-success probability is one, so its correction removes the spurious improvement. This refutes lower-bound subtraction, not the current theorem.

reasoning_steps.title: Concentrate independent task clusters rather than dependent runs
reasoning_steps.argument: Let X_hi=(1/r_h)Σ_j(S_Ahij−S_Bhij), so X_hi∈[−1,1], and D=Σ_h(w_h/n_h)Σ_i X_hi. Under independent clusters, E[D]=d. A centered variable supported on an interval of length 2 has moment-generating function at most exp(λ²/2). Applying this bound to the weighted independent X_hi gives E[exp(λ(D−d))]≤exp(λ²V/2), where V=Σ_h w_h²/n_h. Markov's inequality and minimization at λ=t/V give Pr(D−d≥t)≤exp(−t²/(2V)). Taking t=sqrt(2V log(1/α)) shows d≥D−t with probability at least 1−α. Repetition count r_h does not enter the worst-case radius: perfectly correlated repeats cannot create additional independent tasks.

review.rationale: Each cluster average has range length two. The centered bounded-variable inequality therefore contributes exp(λ²a_hi²/2) for weight a_hi=w_h/n_h. Independence across complete clusters gives Σ_hi a_hi²=Σ_h w_h²/n_h and the stated one-sided tail radius. No independence among repeated runs is required.

reasoning_steps.title: Handle missing judgments conservatively without discarding tasks
reasoning_steps.argument: Define complete certification variables by the fixed judging protocol, whether or not each label is observed. For any missing S_A replace it by 0, and for any missing S_B replace it by 1; known labels remain unchanged. Let D_obs be the resulting weighted cluster difference. Pointwise D_obs≤D, even if missingness is outcome-dependent or correlated across tasks. Therefore the complete-data concentration event also implies d≥D_obs−t. This argument requires a well-defined complete protocol and scheduled denominators. It does not permit deleting missing tasks, silently treating missing truth labels as known, or applying complete-case analysis. A timeout is an actual failure only if the prespecified success rubric makes it one.

review.rationale: Imputing missing intervention certifications as zero and missing baseline certifications as one decreases every affected contrast pointwise. Thus D_obs≤D transfers the complete-data concentration event even under dependent or outcome-related missingness, provided complete certifications and scheduled denominators are well-defined as assumed.

reasoning_steps.title: Combine the bounds and state coverage and edge cases
reasoning_steps.argument: On the event from the preceding steps, Δ≥D_obs−E_err−t and Δ≥−1, establishing the claimed L. For fixed valid allowances, coverage is at least 1−α. If allowances are instead simultaneous upper confidence bounds valid with probability at least 1−β, union bounding gives coverage at least 1−α−β, without requiring calibration and evaluation samples to be independent. Their statistical validity and target-population applicability still require justification. Zero-weight strata may be omitted; positive-weight unsampled strata are outside this theorem. With one cluster the bound remains valid but is usually uninformative. All missing labels give D_obs=−1 and hence L=−1. Multiple mechanisms, endpoints, or interim looks require additional prespecified error allocation; this fixed-comparison result does not cover unrestricted search.

review.rationale: Combining the population correction and concentration event gives the claimed bound, and clipping below at −1 preserves validity. A union bound with a simultaneous allowance-calibration event gives coverage at least 1−α−β without sample independence. The stated all-missing and unsampled-stratum qualifications are consistent with the construction.

reasoning_steps.title: Specify an architectural experiment that can use the guarantee
reasoning_steps.argument: Proposed task family: multi-step ledger workflows requiring exactly one authorized transfer, correct recipient and amount, and a reconciled receipt after a fixed settlement horizon. B uses a fixed bounded-retry policy; A uses the same policy with a stable task-scoped idempotency key and atomic server-side deduplication. Prespecify no-fault, timeout-before-commit, timeout-after-commit, and delayed-response strata and weights. Start each paired execution from an isolated identical snapshot, reset between scheduled runs, and randomize execution order. Hold model/prompt versions and hard token, tool-call, time, and monetary ceilings fixed, including safeguard overhead. The hypothesized benefit is fewer duplicate committed transfers after lost acknowledgments. Test regressions from accidental key reuse, incorrectly suppressed distinct operations, and exhausted budgets separately; these are proposed fault cases, not measured failures.

review.rationale: Accepted as a proposed controlled design under the listed causal-isolation and matched-budget premises, not as implemented evidence. Lost acknowledgment after commit is a discriminating setting for atomic deduplication. Snapshot isolation, overhead accounting, and key-reuse regressions are relevant controls, but their implementation remains open.

reasoning_steps.title: Connect observed outcomes to engineering claims without overclaiming
reasoning_steps.argument: In the proposed controlled environment, evaluate actual terminal ledger state and receipt consistency rather than agent completion claims. An exhaustive outcome oracle would permit η_Ah=ξ_Bh=0 only after its coverage of the declared success predicate is justified; being a separate program is insufficient. Keep delayed unauthorized effects, safe stops, retry counts, latency, and cost as separate prespecified outcomes rather than hiding them in binary success. Stable environment isolation and changing only idempotency handling would support attribution within this task protocol after data collection. Neither the guarantee nor the proposed design establishes benefit on open-ended tasks, shared production state, different budgets, or distribution shifts. The method uses standard bounded-variable concentration; literature novelty and empirical generality are not assessed.

review.rationale: Actual ledger state is more directly connected to the declared outcome than completion claims. A separate oracle program alone does not justify zero truth-error allowances. Attribution remains conditional on genuine isolation and a controlled intervention, and the output correctly withholds measured benefit and cross-domain generalization.
